correctness.rationale: The five Fourier invariants are exact identities verified symbolically and derived in RESULT.md. For nonzero middle coefficient the inverse is precisely a set of common positive roots of two specified monic quadratics satisfying an additional linear identity; two roots occur iff their polynomial equations coincide and the real cross term vanishes. Zero-middle-coefficient and cross-branch cases are fully enumerated, including the zero polynomial, with exact two- and three-class witnesses. Exhaustive algebraic reasoning, not numerical sampling, proves the universal maximum three. Standalone symbolic and direct-sampling checks executed successfully.

value.rationale: The four-node grid is the natural sharp noninjective boundary just below a previously proven five-node universal threshold. Rather than merely giving a counterexample or a modest improvement, the theorem solves the complete inverse-fiber classification on all complex quadratics, including exceptional zero coefficients, two inequivalent ambiguity mechanisms, an unexpected triple fiber, and an explicit reconstruction formula. These exact geometric strata distinguish global injectivity, almost-everywhere injectivity and failure of stability, and are not consequences of generic-frame claims.
